This method projects a 3D Gaussian primitive, defined by a mean and a covariance matrix in world space, into a 2D elliptical footprint (splat) on the image plane for rasterization [S1, S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the method projects a 3D Gaussian primitive (defined by mean and covariance in world space) into a 2D elliptical footprint (splat) on the image plane for rasterization. Source [S1] explicitly describes this process: it reconstructs the 3D covariance from world space parameters, transforms it to eye space, applies a local affine approximation (Jacobian) of the perspective projection to obtain a 2D covariance matrix ($Sigma_{2D}$), and defines the final projected distribution as a 2D Gaussian used for rendering (materializing as an ellipse/splat). Source [S3] corroborates this by stating that 3DGS reuses the EWA splatting projection to map a 3D Gaussian to a 2D elliptical footprint (splat) on the image plane, preserving the Gaussian form through a local affine approximation. Both sources confirm that the 3D Gaussian is defined in world space (or transformed from it) and projected to a 2D footprint for rasterization.

The subjective descriptor 'tight' is not supported by the evidence.
